A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GRACE. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial methodological and empirical revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original BabyAI and Android experiments, including reward recovery, policy learning, sample-efficiency analyses, and goal-identification results.

after.justification: v2 reports original MuJoCo experiments in Table 1 alongside retained BabyAI and Android results.

M1.justification: The thresholded goal/non-goal reward difference in v1 Equation 3.3 becomes a policy-dependent AIRL discriminator objective in v2 Equation 4.1. Mandatory goal identification becomes optional cleaning, and learner trajectories now enter the negative set instead of being relabeled into both sets. Algorithm 1 changes sequential offspring replacement to batch mutation and top-P selection; prompts also remove fixed nonnegative and 100-point goal-reward constraints.

E1.justification: v2 adds continuous-control evaluation on MuJoCo Hopper, Walker, Ant, and Humanoid. The 20 BabyAI levels, including three custom levels, and three AndroidWorld Clock tasks remain. The offline AndroidControl evaluation is now described as timer/stopwatch multitask evaluation rather than the set-alarm scenario specified in v1 Figure 3.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds AIRL with 200 expert trajectories as an evaluated comparator alongside PPO and GAIL. The BabyAI comparator set remains PPO and GAIL. Additional GAIL demonstration budgets are setting changes rather than additional baseline identities.

E3.justification: New MuJoCo protocols evaluate returns, use ten learner-data augmentation rounds, and compare two generator models and different demonstration budgets. The AndroidControl caption changes from eight expert/eight negative trajectories per task to 8–12 expert trajectories and approximately 800 negatives total. Algorithm 1 changes each PPO call's budget from N to N/M, while existing reward-evaluation plots are relabeled as accuracy. These are reported protocol changes, without establishing which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v1 Appendix A.2 and Table 2's goal-identification study, covering input modalities and trajectory shuffling, disappear together with instruction-correction and filtering cases. Sample-efficiency, shaping, module-reuse, and code-evolution analyses remain. v2 additionally compares GPT-4o and Qwen3-Coder-30B generators on MuJoCo.

E5.justification: v2 specifies means and standard deviations across five seeds for the new MuJoCo experiments. Retained convergence plots still report standard-deviation shading across three seeds. This adds run-count information for new experiments, without establishing increased repetition of earlier experiments.

E6.justification: v2 adds MuJoCo returns, including Humanoid scores of 5809 ± 106 for GPT-4o GRACE, 6521 ± 337 for 200-demonstration GAIL, and 6512 ± 291 for AIRL. It removes goal-identification results such as text accuracy 0.94 ± 0.24 versus image accuracy 0.49 ± 0.38. Matched BabyAI success rates remain unchanged; v2 also newly reports qualitatively that eight-demonstration GAIL performs near zero on most BabyAI tasks.

T1.justification: v1's IRL-connection proposition and Appendix A.1 proof are removed. Equation 3.2 reverses the order of policy minimization and reward maximization, and v2 introduces the AIRL discriminator formulation in place of the earlier fitness definition. No replacement theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain sample-efficient reward recovery, interpretable code, useful shaping, and reusable reward APIs. The abstract and introduction extend validation claims to MuJoCo and continuous control. The introductory comparison claim is qualified from outperforming GAIL and ground-truth RL to matching or outperforming baselines and explicitly sparse-reward RL.

C2.justification: v2 adds a feature-statistics explanation of MuJoCo reward generation and attributes Humanoid weakness to difficulty reasoning over large numerical arrays. It removes the earlier Phase 3 labeling-error/generalization tradeoff. The perceptual-input limitation highlighted in the main text already appeared in v1 Appendix A.4. Section 5.2 also extends its all-task baseline interpretation despite the Humanoid exceptions in Table 1.

D1.justification: v2 adds Brax usage, generator-model names, approximately 2000 LLM calls per MuJoCo task, and clearer distinctions between LLM inputs and reward-code inputs. Existing hyperparameter tables remain unchanged. The appendix replaces the broad Clock listing with timer-specific and Hopper examples, revises generation/mutation prompts, and removes the full shaping prompt. The commitment to release code, data, and configurations also disappears; actual availability outside the PDFs is unresolved.

R1.justification: v2 adds AIRL, Brax, and MuJoCo references and removes the GPT-4o system-card reference associated with the deleted study. Related work expands the GAIL/AIRL discussion and explicitly contrasts GRACE with the supervision and pipeline requirements attributed to EUREKA and Code as Reward.

P1.justification: Contributions and mutation feedback become bullet lists, Background becomes separate from Method, and portions of the evaluation narrative are reorganized. Standalone reproducibility and LLM-usage statements disappear. Much of the background, analysis, and appendix discussion retains its earlier wording and organization.

P2.justification: Figure 1 and the algorithm display are revised, a MuJoCo table is added, and the goal-identification table is removed. Appendix Table 3 consolidates previously split BabyAI results without changing their values. Existing plots are relocated, resized, and relabeled, while the visual template and most plot graphics remain.

improvement.justification: MuJoCo evaluation, AIRL comparisons, and five-seed results strengthen empirical validation. However, v2 leaves the connection between its revised AIRL fitness and retained accuracy plots unclear, extends an all-task comparison claim contradicted by Humanoid results, and removes the full prompt for the retained shaping procedure. These empirical benefits and reporting/reproducibility losses do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
